items.followUp: Explain how the position of a moving object changes with respect to its surroundings.

rubric.why: Shows that rest is defined by an unchanged position relative to the surroundings.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an object's position does not change with respect to its surroundings.

rubric.why: Shows that motion is defined by a changing position relative to the surroundings.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an object's position changes with respect to its surroundings.

modelAnswer: A body is at rest if its position does not change with respect to its surroundings.
A body is in motion if its position changes with respect to its surroundings.

items.followUp: Define speed and write its formula.

rubric.why: Identifies acceleration as the change in velocity per unit time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing acceleration as the rate of change of velocity with time.

rubric.why: Gives the formula for acceleration using initial velocity, final velocity and time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

modelAnswer: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with time.

rubric.why: Provides one valid advantage of friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one valid advantage, such as enabling walking, writing or braking.

rubric.why: Provides a second valid advantage of friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a different valid advantage of friction.

modelAnswer: Friction between our feet and the ground enables us to walk without slipping.
Friction between the brakes and a wheel helps a vehicle to stop.

items.followUp: What is the moment arm of a force?

rubric.why: States the defining relationship for torque or moment of a force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that torque is the product of the force and its perpendicular distance from the pivot or axis of rotation.

rubric.why: Gives the SI unit of torque.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for newton metre (N m).

modelAnswer: Torque, or moment of a force, is the product of the force and its perpendicular distance from the pivot or axis of rotation.
Its SI unit is the newton metre (N m).

items.followUp: Define a point mass and describe its motion in a circular path.

rubric.why: Describes a rigid body as one that does not deform, or whose particles remain at fixed distances from one another.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the standard definition of a rigid body.

rubric.why: Identifies the axis as the line about which a body rotates.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining the axis of rotation.

modelAnswer: A rigid body is one whose shape and size do not change when a force is applied; the distance between its particles remains constant.
The axis of rotation is the fixed line about which a body rotates.

rubric.why: Identifies the SI unit of work.
rubric.description: States the SI unit of work.

rubric.why: Defines one joule in terms of the work done by a force through a displacement in its direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that one joule is the work done when a force of 1 N moves an object 1 m in the direction of the force.

modelAnswer: The SI unit of work is the joule (J).
One joule of work is done when a force of 1 N moves an object 1 m in the direction of the force.

items.followUp: Define kinetic energy and give one example.

rubric.why: Defines mechanical energy in terms of a body's motion or position.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that mechanical energy is the energy a body has due to its motion or position.

rubric.why: Gives a valid example of mechanical energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example, such as a moving car having kinetic energy or a raised object having potential energy.

modelAnswer: Mechanical energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion or position.
For example, a moving car has kinetic energy.

items.followUp: Define work and write its SI unit.

rubric.why: Identifies power as how quickly work is done.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining power as the rate of doing work or work done per unit time.

rubric.why: Gives the SI unit of power.

modelAnswer: Power is the rate of doing work.
Its SI unit is the watt (W), where 1 W = 1 J/s.
